messages:
Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: Pager: gpu-serving-prod - pool 'fast-gpu-pool' queue length skyrocketing, eviction throttles observed. initial alert 2359876543. tagging oncall.
Sam Park: seeing huge queue backlog, ~3.8k pending reqs, 95p latency up 4x. autoscaler not adding nodes (hit scale limit?).
Maya Chen: looking now — metrics show driver crashes on some nodes (OOM + CUDA Xid) causing node flaps and effective capacity drop. logs attached below.
Lee O'Connor: can you paste the Xid log lines? suspecting kernel/driver instability rather than workload.
Maya Chen: paste logs:
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:01Z] nvidia: Xid (31) 79 at 0x7f... from GPU 2
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] kernel: GPU driver OOM: process=redwood-infer pid=4123 oom-kill
[2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] kubelet: eviction: pod "infer-svc-abc" terminated due to gpu-kernel-error
```
Sam Park: autoscaler shows pool at max-replicas=18 and we are at 18. backlog growing because autoscale cap reached + several nodes flapped.
Anya Patel: starting mitigation runbook steps: 1) disable batching for high-throughput routes, 2) scale fallback to CPU transformers for non-latency critical customers, 3) cordon affected nodes and cycle driver.
Carter Nguyen: executing cordon/drain on node gpu-07 (flapping). running:
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-07
kubectl drain gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
Maya Chen: thanks. also lowering max-batch-size via config for route /generate to reduce memory pressure. patch applied to envoy route config.
Sam Park: manual scale request to infra: please bump pool quota + provision 4 spare instances (temporary). @Infra Bot can you confirm capacity?
Infra Bot: Received request. Creating ticket to cloud team to request GPU quota increase and spin up 4 instances in region us-west2. ETA 12-15 minutes (cloud quota review).
Support Bot: flagging customers with high error rates: tenant-omega, analytics-inc. Support will notify SLs once we have ETA and mitigation.
Lee O'Connor: aside from autoscaler cap, driver instability is causing kube to mark nodes NotReady intermittently. we should restart driver package on flapped nodes and watch dmesg.
Maya Chen: rolling restart of nvidia-driver on drained nodes now. commands:
```bash
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service || sudo rmmod nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia
journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 50
```
Anya Patel: quick perf tweak: enable prefix KV cache for long-tail chat sessions to reduce token generation on hot routes. patch pushed to runtime config.
Sam Park: observation: after cordon + restart + config changes, queue reduced from 3.8k -> 900 in ~8m. 95p latency down from 2.1s -> 0.9s on sampled routes. still elevated.
Maya Chen: two nodes showed repeated Xid 31 after restart, we've isolated them (gpu-11, gpu-12). marked for hardware review with infra. moving affected nodes to quarantined pool.
Carter Nguyen: temporarily increasing per-tenant throttles to protect control plane and reduce cascading backpressure. applied rate-limits for non-critical customers.
Oncall Bot: :white_check_mark: Action summary: cordoned/drained 1 node, restarted drivers on 4 nodes, disabled batching for hot routes, lowered batch sizes, KV cache enabled, per-tenant throttles applied, manual capacity request submitted.
Support Bot: Drafting status message for impacted customers: brief note + ETA for capacity. will include mitigation steps and ask affected customers to shift to dedicated instances if needed.
Sam Park: recommended follow-ups: 1) increase autoscaler max for pool temporarily, 2) schedule driver rollback to previous vendor release on the nodes that crashed if hardware team approves, 3) run stress tests to reproduce OOM patterns.
Maya Chen: filing a post-incident issue with logs and a playbook addition: check kernel dmesg pattern for Xid 31, and add node health probe to detect early driver OOM signs.
Lee O'Connor: agree. also recommend adding automated fallback routing: when pool capacity drops below threshold, route new requests to cheaper model variants or CPU fallback to keep clients live.
Anya Patel: I'll own the runbook update and the follow-up tests. Sam please own customer comms with Support. Maya + Infra to investigate hardware/driver root cause.
Sam Park: on it. Support will send the initial notice in 10m.
Infra Bot: Cloud request completed: 4 preemptible T4-equivalents scheduled, two ready (gpu-20, gpu-21). provisioning logs: https://infra.internal/requests/CR-4621
Maya Chen: monitoring: backlog now 420 and falling. 95p latency ~0.7s. marking incident as mitigated but not resolved. will keep thread open for RCA.
Oncall Bot: Incident status: mitigated -> partial capacity restored. please update incident doc with timeline.
Support Bot: initial customer notice sent to affected tenants. will send follow-up once hardware team confirms root cause.
Sam Park: thanks all. leaving follow-up tasks in the incident board and assigning owners.
